test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Oct, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: By selling an article for ₹20, a dealer makes a profit of 10%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 45%?
solution:
**Given:**

Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹20

Profit Percentage (P₁%) = 10%

Desired Profit Percentage (P₂%) = 45%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = (SP₁)/(1 + frac{P₁\%){100}}

Selling Price (SP₂) = CP × (1 + (P₂\%)/(100))

Increase in Selling Price = SP₂ - SP₁

**Calculation:**

CP = (20)/(1 + frac{10){100}} = (20)/(1 + 0.1) = (20)/(1.1)

CP = ₹(200)/(11)

SP₂ = (200)/(11) times (1 + (45)/(100)) = (200)/(11) times (1 + 0.45) = (200)/(11) times 1.45

SP₂ = ₹(290)/(11)

SP₂ ≈ ₹26.3636

Increase in Selling Price = SP₂ - SP₁

⇒ Increase = ₹26.3636 - ₹20

⇒ Increase = ₹6.3636

Rounded off to two decimal places, the increase is ₹6.36.

**The dealer should increase his selling price by approximately ₹6.36.**
